title: Blueberry Key Lime Tart with Biscuit Base
changes_from_base: A biscuit-crumb base and a baked lime and condensed milk filling instead of pastry and lemon curd, topped with glossy blueberries.
summary: A lime and condensed milk filling baked on a buttery biscuit base, finished with a thick blueberry topping.
equipment: 23 cm loose-based tart tin or pie dish

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
key lime or ordinary lime juice

steps.title: Crumb case
steps.text: heat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C fan). Stir the crumbs, sugar, salt and melted butter together, then press firmly over the base and up the sides of the tin with the glass.

steps.title: Toast the base
steps.text: bake on the tray for 10-12 min, until lightly browned, then cool on the rack. Turn the oven down to 160 °C (140 °C fan).

steps.title: Filling
steps.text: whisk the yolks, condensed milk, lime juice and zest together until smooth. Pour into the case and bake 18-20 min, just until set with a slight tremble in the middle. The middle firms up more as it cools, so take it out while it still trembles.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: cool at room temperature for 1-2 h before adding the topping.

steps.title: Topping
steps.text: set aside 125 g of the blueberries. Stir the water, sugar, cornflour and lime juice in the pan over medium heat until the sugar dissolves, add the 125 g berries and boil 1-2 min, until glossy and thick.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: pour the hot sauce over the remaining berries, leave 5 min, then spread over the tart to the edges. Chill at least 3 h before slicing.

tips: Press the crumbs firmly so the base holds when sliced.
Bottled key lime juice works well if you cannot find fresh key limes.
Cool the tart fully before topping, or the sauce will slide off.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep well wrapped in the fridge for up to 3 days.
